Though not spectacular at all, it's a good way to start one's travel in Laos and remember that the country has been…

spots.name: The Gibbon Experience
spots.desc: A forest conservation project that raises funds by taking guests into the Bokeo Nature Reserve, home to the Laotian black crested gibbon. Once thought extinct, it is now known that up to 400 people live in this forest. The Reserve is mostly primary monsoon dry deciduous forest, but also contains some lowland slash-and-burn agriculture. The Gibbon Experience is the only way to visit the Reserve.…
spots.price: 2 days/1 night: 1,400,000 kip, 3 days/2 nights: 2,450,000 kip

spots.name: Golden Triangle Special Economic Zone
spots.desc: The provincial economy is now dominated by the Golden Triangle Special Economic Zone (GT SEZ). In 2007, the Chinese-owned Kings Romans Group entered into a 99-year lease for 10,000 hectares on the banks of the Mekong. The company was granted 3,000 of these hectares as a duty-free zone, now the SEZ. As gambling is illegal in China, and the SEZ is only a two-hour journey by road from China, casinos…

spots.name: Morning Market
spots.desc: Pay a visit to the market. The best time to visit is early morning.

spots.name: Daauw Home
spots.desc: Small bar and restaurant run by Project Kajsiab (a non-profit organisation that seeks to improve the health of the Lao people in Bokeo Province). Dinner 70,000-100,000 kip for two; beer, teas and Mojilaos available in the drinks department. Nice setting and chilled vibes around the fire or on the verandah.

spots.name: Khongvab Duck BBQ
spots.desc: For all those tired of chicken and pork. Popular with locals and delicious. From 14:00 to 17:00 when the duck is on the BBQ you can't miss it.

spots.name: Latsuly Return
spots.desc: Restaurant overlooks the slow boat wharf and truck ferry and is a nice place to watch the world go by.

spots.name: No Name
spots.desc: Outdoor restaurant with a big terrace built on the banks of the Mekong. It offers Lao barbecue, a tasty combination of Japanese shabu-shabu and Korean BBQ, i.e., you grill and stew up your own meats and veggies.

spots.name: Green Discovery
spots.desc: Offers up to three-day trekking trips, the price is a bit more expensive than in the tourist office. They also offer kayaking and other activities.

spots.name: Luang Namtha Tourism Department
spots.desc: Offers up to four-day trekking for an average of US$30 per day. Groups can be from 4-8 people and the cost per person drops the more participants there are. Other activities offered include kayaking.

spots.name: The Hiker
spots.desc: The Hiker is a community-based eco-tours travel agency offering premium level adventure tours including trekking, Kayaking, Mountain biking, cultural immersion, in Luang Namtha, Laos.

spots.name: Discoveringlaos
spots.desc: Discovering Laos is a family-held eco-tour operator in Luang Namtha, in the north of Laos, Discovering Laos is owned and managed by Vanxai. The owner has been a guide in the Nam Ha National Park for several years and a trekking coordinator for a major eco-tourism agency in Laos. He opened Namtha River Experience in 2009.

spots.name: Chinese Restaurants
spots.desc: Two Chinese restaurants which are operated by Chinese who speak little English. There is no menu and you can only order by selecting your dishes in their kitchen. Dishes are a bit oily and the serving style is either plain or spicy. The taste is OK and the pricing is far better than at the restaurants in town.

spots.name: Coffee House
spots.desc: Open eatery with a comprehensive Thai menu, lattes and cappuccini, great fruit shakes, plus friendly atmosphere.

spots.name: Lai's Place
spots.desc: Delicious, using fresh ingredients and reasonably priced. Try the peanut Jaeow with sticky rice and vegetables, which is a savoury, herbaceous dip. The fried tofu and vegetables with red curry is very good as well.

spots.name: Minority Restaurant
spots.desc: This little joint is run by a husband and wife from the Black Tai (Tai Dam) tribe and specializes in tribal cuisine, with Tai Dam, Akha and Lisu dishes on offer. The menu also covers banana pancakes, French fries and other dishes for the Western palate. Vegetarian and vegan selections. Boasts "No MSG" in their dishes.

spots.name: Rambo Fusion
spots.desc: Delicious Korean BBQ, popular with locals. A portion (30,000-50,000 kip) serves 2 people.

spots.name: Bamboo Lounge at Forest Retreat
spots.desc: Kiwi-run. Breakfast menu: baked beans, jaffles, best coffee. Offers cocktails. Wi-Fi. Offers trekking and kayak tours.

spots.name: Manychan Guesthouse
spots.desc: Probably the most popular place in town, has a dedicated bar on the 2nd floor above the restaurant.

spots.name: Oudomxay Museum
spots.desc: The museum doesn't have much, but the view you have from the top of "Phou Sebey" mountain is very nice. Go there early in the morning, when the sun is still low. You can watch the town centre waking up and enjoy the morning light as it starts caressing the roofs before the day gets too hot.

spots.name: Phu That Stupa
spots.desc: The stupa was built in the 14th century to allow all people of the region to come together to celebrate religious festivals. When the French came to control the land, the stupa grounds were made into an army camp until independence from France. During the first Vietnamese war the stupa was destroyed and only bricks were left. Reconstruction started in 1994 and finally concluded in 1997. Every…

spots.name: Ban Chom Ong
spots.desc: An outstandingly beautiful village of about 500 people of the ethnic group Khmu. It is starting point to the biggest cave in Northern Laos. Surrounded by rice paddies, locked away by mountains, it is still largely untouched by modern influences. There is no electricity nor mobile phone signal in the village, but as compensation you'll get the chance to observe authentic village life. Handicraft…

spots.name: Nam Heeng
spots.desc: If you're adventurous, it's also possible to reach Ban Chom Ong by going to a village called Ban Nam Heeng first. The village itself is not particularly interesting, but from there it is possible to walk the last 16 km to Chom Ong. So called "packing" cars leave from a special public transport station very near the normal bus station. It costs about 35,000 kip to Nam Heeng. The challenging hike…

spots.name: Nam Kad Waterfall and Forest
spots.desc: While visiting Nam Kad Waterfall, you can not only swim in the ice cold basin under the waterfall, but also see one of the most untouched and beautiful forests in Laos. Rent a motorbike and follow the sign which says "Nam Kad". At a village called "Ban Faen", turn right, and then just follow the road. After some 10-12 km you arrive at a parking lot. Nam Kad is now a privately managed conservation…

spots.name: Hiking
spots.desc: The local Provincial Tourist Office in Muang Xay offers some very nice hiking including night stays in Khamu family homes (not guesthouses), which makes the experience very special and intimate. Although not as colourful as other ethnic groups of Laos, the Khamu people are very nice and happy to have foreigners visit their villages.

spots.name: Banking
spots.desc: There are several banks in the town: BCEL, JDB, Indochina Bank.

spots.name: Chinese Market
spots.desc: Around Luxay Market, Chinese clothing, food, and housewares shops can be found. In contrast to the Lao shops, most of the Chinese shops are open until late at night.

spots.name: Fresh Market
spots.desc: Muang Xay has three fresh food markets: Tin Market, Nonmengda Market, and Phoukhaiw Market. All are excellent places to discover the variety of unique foods that Oudomxay has to offer. Oudomxay has many food items and forest products that are either not available or in scarce supply in other parts of the country. The markets are open every day, however they are particularly colourful on Saturday…

spots.name: Luxay Market
spots.desc: In this market you can find all sorts of products. Upstairs is the clothing and shoes section. Get your daily necessities at the market.

spots.name: Muang Neua Restaurant
spots.desc: International dishes and cocktails in a nice garden atmosphere. Prices are a bit higher than the norm and portions a bit smaller.

spots.name: Souphailin's Restaurant
spots.desc: A broad range of fresh Lao, European and vegetarian dishes. Portions are big, quality excellent, and low prices. The banana-coconut iced coffee, and the curry rice with pineapple and banana are recommended. Be patient with cooking times or order in advance when she has many customers.

spots.name: Oudomxay Night Market
spots.desc: quite a big market square serving grills, hot pots and other Lao and Asian food.

spots.name: Elephant Conservation Center
spots.desc: Come meet elephants displaced from the logging industry or other threats.

spots.name: Elephant Festival
spots.desc: Takes place in Feb every year in a different district. In 2010 was in Hongsa, in 2011 in Pak Lay.

spots.name: AD Learning Centre
spots.desc: A social enterprise providing education, including in English. Similar to Big Brother Mouse in Luang Prabang. Always in need of supplies and volunteers. Drop by! Opposite the check-in restaurant, on the same block as Khamphouy Guest House.

spots.name: Théâtre d'ombres de Champasak
spots.desc: Shadow puppets show on Tuesday and Friday at 8:15pm. 1h15 show for 100.000kip/$5 per adult (free for kids). The story of Ramayana is told in Lao with traditional music played live. The movie Chang is played on Wednesday and Saturday with the soundtrack played live by the musicians. 8:15pm, 1h15 movie for 100.000kip per adult. Some subtitles in English. 📍 Situated next to the tourism office in…

spots.name: Omany BBQ
spots.desc: Serves Lao-style hotpot with fish or meat.

spots.name: Massage
spots.desc: The Lao Red Cross offer very good massages.

spots.name: Toukta Bakery & Café
spots.desc: Also sells reasonably-priced Thai food.

spots.name: Champasak eSPAce bien-etre
spots.desc: Coconut oil massages on the riverbank.

spots.name: Ethnic Villages
spots.desc: Take a guided tour by one of the local operators or hop on a bicycle for a full-day exploring Muang Sing town environs. On a tour you will visit 8-10 villages and learn about the rural life of different ethnic groups. The China border is only 10 km from town and makes for a refreshing journey on a bicycle. You can't cross the border, however the scenery along the way is beautiful and worth the…

spots.name: The Muang Sing Market
spots.desc: The heart of the town and attracts people from the entire region to buy fresh foods and products for daily use imported from China. Best time to visit the market is between 07:00-08:00: retailers from all the ethnic groups arrive to sell vegetables, fruit, and meat, and Tai Lue women present their famous noodles. It's also a great place to look for local handicrafts purchased by Tai Dam, Tai Lue…

spots.name: Muang Sing Museum
spots.desc: Close to the centre of town, is a good place to start exploring Muang Sing's rich culture and history. The old wood and brick building was once the residence of Phanya Sekong, a local lord called Jao Fa Noi or Little Prince, who ruled over the area in the early 20th century. The building was restored in 2005. Due to its functional structure the façade was refinished, but the clay roofing tiles…
spots.price: 5,000 kip (plus 5,000 kip extra for the Akha film)

spots.name: Scenery & Nature in Muang Sing
spots.desc: Nam Keo Waterfall: nature lovers will enjoy this place. The multi-tiered Nam Keo Waterfall is about 2 km from That Xieng Tung and can be visited as part of a guided tour from the Muang Sing Ecoguide Service or while on the Akha Experience. Pha Yueng Waterfall is a good place for a refreshing dip. It is in Nam Ha National Protected Area, 17 km south of Muang Sing on the road to Luang Namtha.…

spots.name: Temples & Monasteries
spots.desc: In Muang Sing more than 27 temples (wats), that the old wat is Vat Xieng Chai (Wat Luang). The most important wat in the area is off the main road next to the museum. By 1890 only Wat Luang existed within the town walls. Wat Namkeo, which has a large monk residency, is a short walk from the fort. It is also quite beautiful and is on the road to Xieng Kok, just as you turn off from the paved road…

spots.name: That Xieng Tueng
spots.desc: The most important stupa in Muang Sing. It is said to contain the Adam's apple of Buddha. The date of when it was built is unknown. To the left of the stupa are some stairs which lead to a sacred fountain and a sacred stone. If you follow a path to the right of the stupa (be careful!) downhill you might be able to find the old moat and wall of the stupa. The biggest festival of the year, That…

spots.name: Xieng Khaeng Mountains & Upper Mekong
spots.desc: Xieng Khaeng is a largely unexplored, stunning region with beautiful mountains, waterfalls and caves, embedded between mountains and the Mekong River. Only a couple of hours from Muang Sing town, the Akha and Tai Lue villages in this remote area have still kept their traditions and culture. Access to Xieng Khaeng is difficult and a local guide is required. The northern-most extreme of the Mekong…

spots.name: Muang Khong Market
spots.desc: You have get up and early if you want to head to the main market in Don Khong. A variety of fresh Mekong fish are sold along with palm sugar, leaf hats and other produce.

spots.name: Phou Bia
spots.desc: Highest mountain in Laos (2,830m), close to the capital. Might become accessible with the new tourism efforts in the province.

spots.name: Nam Ngum 2 Hydroelectric Power Project
spots.desc: Dam and lake upstream from the Nam Ngum 1 dam. Road 9308 south from Ban Nongpou offers gorgeous views onto the lake from above, but does not lead straight to the shore of the lake (unlike indicated on some maps). To get to the shore from the west, either take road Nr. 5 from Tha Heua, or a side road in Naxay Savang. Completed in 2011 and the lake now covers some villages and roads that are still…

spots.name: Nang Phone Home Cave
spots.desc: Cave system signposted on the roadside from Pha Tang towards Ban Xuang. Has sections to explore on foot and a river passing through that you can swim in.

spots.name: Tad Namsamam
spots.desc: A waterfall, 3 km from town, following an upstream jungle path with plenty of rocks to climb and possibilities of swimming. Perfect for a one-day trek, with or without local guide. The path starts at the left side of the only temple in town. Leave before noon, so you won't get lost in the dark. Beware of mosquitoes and elephants. The Tourist Centre will sell you a ticket for 15,000 kip, but this…

spots.name: Vieng Xai Caves
spots.desc: Discover the “hidden city”. There are tours to the caves in English every day at 09:00 and 13:00 (60,000 kip). You can also take a tour at other times during Visitor Centre open hours for an extra 50,000 kip per group. During the low season, there may only be a handful of visitors, so you may even acquire a personal tour and move from cave to cave with the tour guide on his scooter. The Visitor's…
spots.price: 60,000 kip for foreigners, 20,000 kip for locals and nationals of Vietnam and China

spots.name: Trekking
spots.desc: Mr. Khamman offers 1-4 day trekking tours to the hill tribes around Muang Khua (information and contact info can be found at several guest houses and the restaurant at the main intersection)

spots.name: Restaurant with unknown name
spots.desc: On the main intersection is an attractive restaurant. The ice cream is popular with locals

spots.name: Market
spots.desc: There are at least two stalls selling tasty bowls of noodle soup across from the market. 10,000 kip. In the market itself you will find a range of grilled meat, fruit and other local staples.

spots.name: Tham Kang Cave and Tham Pha Kaew Cave
spots.desc: These caves were bomb shelters during the Vietnam War. North of town, about 50 min by foot and can be found without a guide. There is a 10,000 kip toll to enter, to see the village, or to walk past the village. It is claimed this money is for a bridge but if you demand a ticket you will see it is for the cave only and can refuse to pay if you wish. Continue past the caves for about 45 min to…

spots.name: Nam Ou Beach
spots.desc: At the end of the dry season when the water is low, take a cool splash in the Nam Ou or sip from a cocktail on a bamboo chaise longue.

spots.name: Phetdavanh Book Exchange
spots.desc: Change your old books for new ones at this 2-for-1 book exchange with more than 300 titles.

spots.name: Visit Surrounding Villages
spots.desc: There are guest houses in all 3 villages, costing 50-100k kip for a bungalow.

spots.name: Phanoy Lookout Point
spots.desc: A steep climb leading to a lookout platform with great views over Muang Ngoi, the Nam Ou and the surrounding mountains. There are two trails and the signs suggest you go up the left hand trail and down the right, however, the left hand trail consists mainly of limestone rock, and bamboo rails, though often loose and shakey, have been installed for safety and easier climbing. The left hand route…

spots.name: Phaboom Lookout Point
spots.desc: If the Phanoy Lookout Point doesn't cut it and you're up for a little challenge, you can ascend the limestone mountain immediately south of Muang Ngoi. There will be a villager collecting the entrance fee right at the gate. The first hour is a steep, slippery climb, with plenty of roots serving as steps, and there are ropes for assistance. You'll come out at an average lookout point with limited…

spots.name: Street stalls
spots.desc: There are a couple of street stalls selling bbq sticks, or fried goodies such as battered bread (2k), coconut battered banana (1k), and fried taro and coconut balls (1k), and bags of banana chips (5k) and fried riverweed (10k). The riverweed in particular is very tasty when fried and much cheaper than in the restaurants, it also goes particularly well with beer so if you've snagged yourself a…

spots.name: Aloune Mai
spots.desc: Good Lao food and cold Beerlao. Makes its own bread and pizza dough. Closed during off season.

spots.name: Lattanavongsa Restaurant
spots.desc: Solid and clean. Boasts big wooden balcony and marble table seats on the grass.

spots.name: Nicksa's Place
spots.desc: Nicksa's Place has 2 restaurants, 50 m away from each other on the main road. The furthest one offers good prices and a very quiet view on the river.

spots.name: Ning Ning Restaurant
spots.desc: Big open-air terrace overlooking the Nam Ou. Best view in town.

spots.name: Phetdavanh Guesthouse
spots.desc: All-you-can-eat breakfast buffet. Food in buffet is not anything special but good quantity for the money. 2 cocktails for 1 during happy hour. First house on the main street with a stone step.

spots.name: Vita Restaurant
spots.desc: Run by a friendly local couple. Deck with nice wooden tables and chairs, but not much other decoration. Free WiFi. While the menu is not as extensive as other restaurants in town and the atmosphere is lacking, the food is of fine quality and good value for money.

spots.name: Bee Tree Bar
spots.desc: Nice spot completely at the long end of the main road on the left. Bar with stools, couches and fireplace. Great Italian red wine.

spots.name: Gecko Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: A nice bar/restaurant, good (if not the same every day) music selection. Friendly owner and staff. 20,000 kip for a cocktail during the happy hour. Their Lao food (or Lam, Suzy, etc.) is also great, ask for spicy (if you can tolerate it) for a more authentic experience.

spots.name: Pha Tok Caves
spots.desc: This cave, set high in a limestone cliff, sheltered villagers and Pathet Lao fighters during the Second Indochina War. The caves are reached via steep concrete steps, and inside a few signs identify points where command posts were stationed. Entrance fees are collected at the bottom where you can also borrow a torch. The trail to the cave passes through many rice paddies and a small section of…

spots.name: Ban Man Da
spots.desc: This is a small village 2km south of Nong Khiaw. It has a mini "Secret War" Museum, a Cave, and a nice little restaurant.

spots.name: Phadaeng Viewopint
spots.desc: Probably the most well-known viewpoint in the area. The viewpoint to see a 360-degree view of the town and surrounding mountains. Entrance is well signed about 500 m east of the bridge. Takes 1-1½ hr to reach the top. Perfect sunrise/sunset spot.

spots.name: Nang None Mountain / Sleeping Woman Viewpoints
spots.desc: There are two viewpoints. North side of the river. Climbing takes around 1.5 hours. Quite a tough climb. Recommended for experienced trekker.

spots.name: Som Nang Viewpoint
spots.desc: The climb takes a little more than 30 mins. Probably the easiest hiking trail in the area.

spots.name: Pha Noi & Pha Kao Viewpoints
spots.desc: The ticket covers two viewpoints, with Pha Noi being the easier one, about 35 minutes to climb, and Pha Kao the harder trail, takes around 2 hours to climb.

spots.name: Phar Kew Lom Viewpoint
spots.desc: Peak height of 1088m. Climb time 2 hr. A challenging hiking trail.

spots.name: BCEL Bank
spots.desc: Good exchange rates. Traveller's cheques accepted and an ATM. There are two BCEL ATMs, one on the bank branch on the West side of the bridge, and one more on the East end of the bridge, near the Riverside Resort intersection. An easy way to get cash up before going to Muang Ngoi.

spots.name: Mama Alex Restaurant
spots.desc: Long time favourite with tourists. Cheap cozy place with delicious Laos and Western food. Fantastic and friendly hostess.

spots.name: CT Restaurant
spots.desc: Offers fine views from its riverside terrace. Free Wi-Fi. Lao coffee here is particularly good.

spots.name: Chennai
spots.desc: A great Indian restaurant (better than Deen) with a veg and non veg tali that can feed two people for 30,000 kip. Great shakes and Lao coffee. Free wifi.

spots.name: Deen Restaurant
spots.desc: Indian food. The portions of the set meals (veg/non veg 20,000/25,000 kip) are not very big and are insufficient if you are quite hungry. Wi-Fi.

spots.name: Delilah's
spots.desc: A selection of everything home made including ice cream, bread, soups and salads. No MSG or additives used. Laos Western fusion cuisine with a creative twist. Also a nice meetingplace in the evening. It also has some dorm beds upstairs.

spots.name: Nong Kiau Riverside Eco-lodge
spots.desc: Very good Lao, Asian and Western food. Beautiful view over the river. Prices a little higher than other restaurants nearby.

spots.name: Vongmany restaurant
spots.desc: Tasty Lao food. Try their local dish "Jeow Mak Len" (a small bowl of Lao style pan-fried tomatoes, herbs and spices accompanied by steamed vegetables for dipping. A healthy starter or light snack. Very popular with locals. 15,000 kip).

spots.name: Coco Home Bar & Restaurant
spots.desc: Bar & restaurant serving authentic Thai and Western dishes by a Thai chef. Full range of cocktails, mixers and shots. Movies shown at 08:00, 12:00, and 18:00 every day on big balcony with river-mountain views. Two raised chill out huts and a comfy hideaway inside. Free Wi-Fi, satellite TV, message board, and blankets available all night.

spots.name: Bay First
spots.desc: Good Thai-Lao food. Friendly owner/chef with 15 years cooking experience in Bangkok.

spots.name: Mekong Elephant Camp
spots.desc: A non-riding Elephant Sanctuary in Pakbeng with an environmental purpose

spots.name: Hive Bar
spots.desc: Offers some music to dance to and seems to stay open later than the other bars.

spots.name: Pheksokxai Lodge
spots.desc: Has very basic rooms with a non-functioning TV, but the lodge has a fantastic pavilion, great views of the river and the mountains as well as a great balcony, plus a nice restaurant with spicy noodles and bamboo shoots.

spots.name: Tourism Information and Trekking Guide Service Centre
spots.desc: Often closed as all the guides are primarily farmers and turn up only if trekkers are on sight!

spots.name: Bus Stop Restaurant
spots.desc: Good fried noodles. Lots of dishes and English menu. Nice, friendly staff.

spots.name: Nang Sone
spots.desc: A nice restaurant in the south of town. Has English menu. Food is nice.

spots.name: Swim in the Mekong River
spots.desc: There is a little beach where boats drop people off, or it's possible to swim in the waters in front of most of the guesthouses. There are even little fish in the water, which nibble off dead foot skin, if you keep still enough. Be careful! Currents can be very strong, and jumping in the river is not recommended if you are not a confident swimmer. Just like in the ocean, if you do get caught in a…

spots.name: Tubing
spots.desc: Rent a tube and float in the Mekong river for a few hours. 10k for a tube, and another 15,000 kip if you want to be driven out a bit by boat. Bring some drinks and have fun.

spots.name: Hang out at the "beach"
spots.desc: Have a drink at the Garden of Nang, a small sandy private beach open to anyone who makes a purchase at the friendly locally-run restaurant across the street. Located on the southwest shore of the island near the bridge to Don Khon.

spots.name: Li Phi Falls
spots.desc: Visit Li Phi Falls, 2 km south of the French railway bridge that connects Don Det and Don Khon.

spots.name: Chao Anouvong’s Cave
spots.desc: Close to the capital.

spots.name: Long Tieng
spots.desc: Town and secret air base during the Vietnam War.

spots.name: Meen Indian Restaurant
spots.desc: Tasty Indian and Lao food.

spots.name: Pha Mery Viewpoint
spots.desc: The climb should take about 2 hours.
spots.price: Entrance is further south of the town.

spots.name: Sunset Restaurant
spots.desc: Reasonable prices for the food, and river view.

spots.name: Welcome Home
spots.desc: Little restaurant. Has nice view of the Chook River.

spots.name: Tad Fan waterfall
spots.desc: A big waterfall over 100m high

spots.name: Waterfalls
spots.desc: Go see waterfalls on Don Khon island.

spots.name: Seng Ahloune Restaurant
spots.desc: Pretty extensive menu at good prices. Food is fine.

spots.name: Nong Sack Restaurant
spots.desc: Good massamam curry and breakfast fare. Reasonable prices.
